analysis.title: Steel Dynamics Inc. (STLD): New $3bn Authorization Supports Shareholder Returns
key_insights: After the close on 11/9, STLD's Board authorized an additional $3.0bn share repurchase program, effective immediately and additive to the prior $1.5bn authorization, which had $216mn remaining as of 9/30. Total repurchase authorization is now ~$3.2bn.
The Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.53/share, payable on or about January 8, 2027 to shareholders of record as of December 31, 2026.
GS views the announcement as supportive for the equity and reiterates its Buy rating with a 12-month price target of $299, about 31.4% above the $227.56 price.
GS estimates that if buybacks run at the historical ~45% of earnings, there could be +8%/+12% upside to consensus EPS in 2027/2028 at the current share price.
GS largely expected an additional authorization given STLD's capital return framework. It currently models $880mn/$800mn of repurchases in 2027/2028.
STLD has historically returned ~45% of net income through buybacks, while GS models ~30% of net income returned. GS sees potential for near-term upside to buybacks.
STLD reduced its share count by ~13% over the last 3 years.
GS currently sees 6%/8% upside to consensus EPS in 2027/2028 from its own estimates. At a 45% payout it sees an incremental ~2%/~3% upside to GSe 2027/2028 EPS.
The price target rests on a 10x EV/EBITDA multiple applied to average FY2026E-FY2028E EBITDA.

market_movers.rationale: The new $3.0bn buyback authorization adds capacity for repurchases, which GS views as supportive. Buybacks at the historical ~45% of earnings would lift EPS 8%/12% above consensus in 2027/2028.

earnings_insights: GS EPS estimates (basis not stated in the report, GS forecasts): $17.53 for 12/26E, $23.35 for 12/27E, $20.97 for 12/28E. Reported FY2025 EPS was $8.00.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: $5.26 for 9/26, $5.79 for 12/26E, $6.23 for 3/27E, $5.74 for 6/27E.
GS sees 6%/8% upside to consensus EPS in 2027/2028. Buybacks at ~45% of net income would give 8%/12% upside to consensus EPS (GS estimate, not a reported figure).
risk_factors: Slower than expected ramp of the aluminum business.
Increases in domestic capacity could pressure prices downward.
Slower-than-anticipated economic growth could decelerate US steel demand.
